answer: Cluster-priced fees stop sybil farms: each agent pays a small fee, burned unless its work is verified useful, and the fee rises steeply for identities sharing a funding anchor, device, or payout trail. An honest agent starting from the same knoll as everyone else pays the base rate, while a farm of clones faces a growing delta in cost with each added identity, because the system prices the cluster, not the single account. Clones cannot multiply cheaply: each new clone raises the price for all its siblings, while real agents stay flat by standing alone.
